turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on comparatives (-er, more ... than)?
turns.tutor:
Here's the rule: short words add -er (easy - easier); long words use more; then than.
Right: "A horse is heavier than a dog." Wrong: "A horse is heavyer than a dog." Heavy ends in y, so the y changes to i before -er.
Let me think aloud: "A tiger is more dangerous than a cat." Dangerous is a long adjective, so I use more, then than.
Your turn. First decide: is the word short or long? Then fill the gap:
Complete: "Cairo is ___ (big) than Luxor."
